title: Fixed Curved Serrated Blade and Palm Grip Rocker
description: One newly authored complete static mezzotint-rocker-inspired hand tool. A single broad finite steel-look plate has a curved front edge with thirty-six actual finite-thickness serrations and a continuous bevel strip following every tooth and valley. Both shoulders narrow into one rising root and tang seated in a complete short rounded wooden-look palm grip; one whole thick annular alloy-look ferrule surrounds that root. Full blade back and a finite grip facet rest at the same ground datum. All numerical outlines, serrations, shoulder/root transitions and grip proportions are new, not an old U-flute gouge, bent hive scraper or long pen handle reused. Four opaque PBR roles, metre scale, native Z up, one whole model zero scenes. Broad printmaking-tool appearance only; coarse visual serrations are not a real working tooth specification. No sharpened edge, cutting, plate preparation, ink retention, printing performance, historical maker, manufacture, ergonomics, strength or safety capability. Fixed intentional assembly overlaps; no animation, rig or interaction.
